timeline.title: A Short History of Staying Close
items: The Penny Black, the world's first sticky postage stamp, made it easy to post a letter to someone far away.
Alexander Graham Bell made the first telephone call, and distance suddenly felt a lot smaller.
Ray Tomlinson sent the first email between two computers. Love letters would never be the same.
The United States named a National Grandparents Day, thanks to the hard work of Marian McQuade.
today: A whole newspaper, posted with love, because some news is too special for a text.

letters.title: What the World Has Said About Love Across the Miles
items: The distance is nothing when one has a motive.
Elizabeth Bennet, in Pride and Prejudice by Jane Austen
Children's children are a crown to the aged.
Grandparents sort of sprinkle stardust over the lives of little children.
Absence makes the heart grow fonder.
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: we miss you, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of Missing Someone
items: Wherever we are, we all see the same face of the Moon. Look up tonight and we are looking too.
One study found a loved one's voice on the phone calmed children almost as much as a hug.
Smell is wired close to the brain's memory centres, so one sniff can take you right back.
Killer whale grandmothers lead their pods to food and help their grandchildren survive.
Elephant herds are led by older females whose memory guides the family to water in hard times.
Some scientists think grandparents helping with children is one reason humans live so long.
facts.hand: So far away, and still so close to our hearts.

world.kicker: A thank you from all of us
world.title: Why the World Is Better With You in It
world.lead: Because of you, the world got:
items: The warmest hug at the end of a long journey.
Stories that keep our family history alive.
A kitchen where the biscuit tin is never empty.
Someone who thinks every drawing is a masterpiece.
Patience that could outlast any rainy day.
A love that travels further than any post.
And the best {who} we could ever have asked for.
world.close: The world is better because of you, {who}. Ours most of all.

promises.title: Our promises to you
items: To call you, even when nothing happened.
To save our best hugs for your visit.
To send drawings, photos and news.
To keep your stories and pass them on.
To love you, always, however far away.

cert: The Most Missed Person in the World
perfume: Top notes of warm toast, old photo albums and garden roses. A heart of pure gold.

note.title: What we believe family is
paras: We make magazines and newspapers for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
We believe distance is just a number. Love finds its way through phone calls, parcels and paper, and it arrives every time, a little warmer than it left.
{who}, someone wanted you to have something special. Not a quick message on a screen, but real pages you can hold, full of news, faces and little voices from home.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, you are missed more than you could ever know.
note.wish: Until the next big hug, {who}. We love you.

sig.intro: Everything {forWho} missed this week, in one place.

weave.text: The big news first, because it could not wait. {headline}. Reporters at the scene describe the mood as delighted, loud and missing you.
There is an empty chair at the table that nobody ever quite gets used to. What everyone misses most is {miss|low}. Distance is long. Love is longer.
Overheard in the kitchen this week: {quote|low}. The family stands by every word.
Some memories live in your nose. Ask anyone and they will tell you that the house smells of {s_house|low}. It is the smell of being safe and fed and loved.
The lesson that stuck? {s_taught}. It gets passed on now, at every meal, to people who were not even born when it was first said.
And when the day comes, the plan is already made. {s_visit}. Then probably more of the same.
